source.title: H. Dilpriya’s Momentum (HDM): A Multi-Strategy Gradient-Aligned Optimizer with Adaptive Per-Parameter Corrections, Cosine-Annealed Scheduling, and Convergence Guarantees for Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper. Some equations and symbols are garbled in the extracted text, but the optimizer comparison tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out classification accuracy for several optimizers on MNIST and CIFAR-10, using different tasks and methods from the optimizer comparisons in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer results on natural-label classification tasks, but does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, architectures against each other, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples. Optimizer settings were tuned for best performance on each benchmark, so the limited-tuning condition in V4 is not established. Gradient-alignment measurements are not measures of the train–test gap.
record.test_reason: Tables III–IV compare Adam and RMSprop with SGD and momentum SGD on held-out image classification accuracy, bearing on V4 in these settings. The tuning search and budget are unspecified, so the limited-tuning condition and the effects of broader tuning cannot be established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the classification conclusion: HDM ranks second on MNIST and CIFAR-10, while Adam leads CIFAR-10. The authors additionally claim superior gradient alignment and strongly convex convergence guarantees. They do not establish a controlled limited-tuning comparison. Their claim of zero MNIST generalization gap is incorrect: 100% training accuracy versus 98.22% test accuracy gives a 1.78 percentage-point gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates HDM, comparing optimizers on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Baseline hyperparameters were set according to original papers and tuned for best performance on each benchmark; this differs from V4's limited-tuning comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture differ between the MNIST MLP and CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, and optimizer rankings vary between these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: YellowFin, DEAM, and the proposed HDM have varying accuracy rankings against SGD and momentum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-alignment methods and automatic momentum tuning can change held-out accuracy relative to fixed SGD recipes.

record.peer_reviewed: 2026 4th International Conference on Advanced Network Technologies and Applications (APAN); the supplied text also identifies the work as posted July 13th, 2026.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the classification results. Only two image-classification datasets are tested. The authors state that baseline optimizer hyperparameters were tuned for best performance on each benchmark; the text does not give a common tuning budget or establish the limited-tuning condition in V4. The convergence theorem is for strongly convex objectives, while the neural-network tasks are non-convex.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for training time, gradient-alignment statistics, synthetic convex optimization, or ablations: these do not measure held-out classification performance for V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.

A verified learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning protocol; controlled limited-versus-broader tuning; language models; decoupled weight decay; switching Adam to SGD. MNIST adaptive methods also have worse training accuracy, so equal-or-better training performance is not demonstrated there.
Batch-size sweeps, fixed-epoch batch penalties, and mitigating recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Classification table values match the record. Results use one fixed seed, with no uncertainty estimates; claims about statistical noise are unsupported by reported replication. Gradient cosine similarity is not V7 sharpness. Comparing an MLP on MNIST with ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 does not test V3 because architecture and dataset change together.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Limited-tuning conditions, broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay, and word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and comparing with random-example removal.
